    ML readiness

    Two baseline models, cross-validated (5 folds), to show how predictable each output is from the inputs before a real model is trained: a quadratic ridge regression and a distance-weighted k-NN (k = 8). The terminal centre enters as sin/cos of 1, 2, 3 and 6 × angle. Importance = loss of R² when one input is shuffled (best model).

    Input importance

    share of the R² lost when the input is shuffled

    binned median with the interquartile band, over all other inputs

    Predicting feasibility

    every rule margin predicted out of fold (best of ridge / k-NN); a design is called feasible when all predicted margins are ≥ 0

    Predicting each rule's margin

    best of ridge / k-NN (named under each rule), out of fold; “sign right” = pass/fail predicted correctly

    Data dictionary

    Dataset checks

    The solver itself is verified in the study page (Kirchhoff, Tellegen, reciprocity, coil resistance). These checks are on the dataset.

    Method

    Sampling. Latin hypercube over every input in the dictionary, one hypercube per worker process with its own seed, so the union is still space filling. Terminal angles: the middle terminal's angle, an order (6 permutations) and two gaps, each ≥ 10° with their sum ≤ the allowed span. Positions move only inside the free radial room. Nothing is filtered on the outputs: every sample is solved and kept.

    Model. The same code as the pages: DC nodal network at 360 A rms line (208 A phase), copper at 20 °C, 10 µΩ welds and 20 µΩ bolts, delivered v7 coil path. Rules as on the pages at the baseline (96 V, overmould insulation, strain 25 %, span 35°, pitch 15 mm, J 12 A/mm², path 4 %, line-line 1.5 %, 2 mm inside the OD).

    For ML. Train on the input columns; predict the outputs and the m_* margins (positive = pass) rather than the pass flag alone, so a new limit can be applied without retraining. Treat centre as an angle (sin/cos). Imbalance depends on where the terminals sit relative to the 12 coil leads, so it is periodic and less smooth than copper or loss; tree ensembles or a small neural network should beat the baselines here.

    Rerun. python opt/dataset_v7.py [N_multi] [N_single] then python opt/make_dataset_pages_v7.py.
